Base-table ownership and classification, as data. This file is the single enforcement source consumed by the hgcrossmodule analyzer (ADR-0039 D1: a module emitting raw SQL against a table another module owns is a violation).

COMPLETENESS IS THE POINT (#87/A1 review F1). This file used to hold only the tables whose ownership had already come up - 37 of the 56 live base tables. hgViolation treats an unknown table as a non-violation, so every omitted table was an unguarded table: a foreign `UPDATE document_images ...` was invisible and nothing failed. The old parity test walked catalog -> docs, a direction that cannot see an omission. `tables` below is now the COMPLETE base-table universe of the governed schema, and table_ownership_completeness_test.go proves it in both directions against db/baseline + db/migrations. Omission is not a classification: a live base table that is not here is a red build.

CLASSES. Every live base table carries exactly one.
  module       - owned by one enforcement module (internal/modules/<owner>); foreign raw SQL is a violation.
  platform     - cross-cutting by architectural design, no module owner, so there is no foreign access to define.
  historical   - in the schema with no live owner; recorded, not enforced. Currently empty: every live base table has a governed owner. The class exists so that a future dead table gets classified instead of omitted.
  out-of-scope - deliberately outside H-G enforcement, with the reason stated.

`retired` is the other half of the parity: tables that wiki/database/tables still documents but the live schema no longer has. Naming them here lets the doc set and the schema be reconciled mechanically instead of by reading, and gives `document_attachments` an answer that is checked rather than remembered.

This file is NOT a second truth. table_ownership_parity_test.go asserts, on every `go test ./...`, that each entry agrees with wiki/database/tables/<table>.md ('**Owner:** <module>') after alias normalisation. Where the governed doc labels a table with something that is not a module directory under internal/modules/, the entry must record that label verbatim in wiki_owner - an explicit, reviewable divergence rather than a silent one.

Owner values are the top-level directory name under internal/modules/. 'Top-level' matters: iam/presence is inside iam, so a read across sub-packages of one module is not cross-module.

tables.note: Live base table with a governed doc, omitted from this catalog until the F1 completeness pass - exactly the shape reverse completeness now makes impossible. TestHGCrossModule_Positive_ForeignWriteToPreviouslyOmittedTable is its negative fixture.

Created by archive/migrations/0070 for the MDDM shadow-diff comparison; no Go code references it today. Kept module-owned rather than classified historical: it is in the live schema, the governed doc names an owner, and enforcing it costs nothing.
approval's signature-reauth limiter; the governed doc agrees despite the auth_ prefix.
The governed doc names a product surface rather than a module; iam owns the writes (internal/modules/iam/infrastructure/postgres/tenant_data_port.go).

The doc labels the tenant registry auth/platform. Enforced as auth-owned rather than left unenforced: several modules read it and those reads are recorded in the cilint baseline as #93/A4 debt, but a NEW foreign WRITE to the tenant registry is rejected from today.

ADR 0044: the domain-event sink is audit-owned. approval INSERTs into it and iam DELETEs from it; both are foreign writes, and recording the writer as the owner (the pre-B4 state) made them invisible to the A4.0 census.
The doc names a path inside render rather than a module directory; render is the enforcement owner.
Same divergence as notifications: the doc labels the outbox family platform/workers, and render is the only module emitting SQL against this dispatch outbox.
The governed doc labels this a platform concern rather than a module; enforcement needs a module directory, and internal/modules/jobs is where the store lives.
The governed doc labels the whole outbox/worker family platform/workers; the notifications module owns this table's writes.

The transactional-outbox invariant makes every module a writer by design (state-write and side effect share one tx; internal/platform/outbox is the writer). No module owns it, so there is no foreign access to define. Classified, not omitted.
Written by the migration runner under db/, never by module SQL. Deliberately outside H-G enforcement; no file under internal/modules references it.
